# vita-memio 1.4.0

This release makes **Read ahead learn how each game reads** and turns it on by default as **Adaptive**. It also measures how much read ahead saves on your own console (**Tuning**), adds **DMA copy**, and splits the overlay and the HUD into a module of their own, so they use no memory when switched off.

**There is a new file, `vitamemio_hud.skprx`.** Copy it to `ur0:tai/` together with the other two; it does not go in `config.txt`. See *Install or update* below.

## New

**Read ahead: Adaptive** (the new default). Read ahead now has three choices: *Off*, *On* and *Adaptive*. Adaptive starts where *On* does and, while you play, works out from how the game reads when read ahead pays off best, and switches to it:

- for large reads, after 2 to 8 reads in a row (*On*: 5);
- for reads of 32 KiB in a row, after 4 to 32 reads (*On*: 16);
- for very small reads in a row, from which one the plugin reads a block of the file at once, and how big (8, 16 or 32 KiB).

Each kind is worked out on its own, for cached memory and for graphics data apart, and it reacts within the first second or two of a loading screen. What it has learned for a game is kept until the console restarts (for the last eight games), so a game you come back to goes on from there.

**Tuning** (in the overlay, *Auto* by default). The plugin measures, for each storage, how much time read ahead saves on your console and what a read for nothing costs. Once it has measured enough, Adaptive and the R/A Test use these figures instead of the standard ones. They are saved to `ur0:data/vita-memio/` only when they change noticeably, so the internal storage is rarely written to. *Triangle* on the line, twice, forgets what was measured.

**DMA copy** (*Advanced*, on by default). Copying from the plugin's buffers to the game is done by the console's DMA controller instead of the CPU, in about half the time. It switches itself off if anything goes wrong.

**GPU-safe reads** now has three choices: *Off*, *Non-DMA* (new default: not after DMA copy's copies, which write memory directly) and *All*. If a game shows graphics glitches, use *All*.

## Changed

- **New defaults:** Read ahead *Adaptive* (was Off), Overlay *On* (was Off), Small transfers *On* (was Off), DMA copy *On*, GPU-safe reads *Non-DMA* (was on for every read), Statistics *Off* (was On). Your storage itself still starts switched off.
- **The overlay and the HUD are a module of their own** (`vitamemio_hud.skprx`), loaded by the plugin only when *Overlay* is on. With it off, none of their code, fonts or buffers take kernel memory. Switching *Overlay* off takes effect at once.
- **HUD:** no setting of its own any more; it is part of the overlay. A new line shows where read ahead starts now for large, 32 KiB and very small reads (for example `C:5:2/16/3`), with **Auto** in green while Tuning measures. A **B** shows whether the game's buffers could be used for copying on the spare core. The HUD is the same size in every game.
- **R/A Test:** not shown while Read ahead is *Adaptive*, which works this out by itself. While the test runs, read ahead uses the standard 5 and 5.
- **The internal storage option is gone.** It holds the system's own data, so it is never sped up; the plugin no longer touches it or game cards at all. A settings file with it on loads with it off.
- **Less memory:** smaller thread stacks, and the HUD and overlay only when switched on.
- **Fewer writes to the internal storage:** the boot guard now writes one byte in place instead of creating and deleting a file at every start.
- **Copy on the system core** now also takes game buffers whose first page lies outside any memory block; that part is copied on the game's core.
- **The log** is shorter and no longer has debugging lines.

## Fixed

- **The HUD and the overlay no longer blink.** They are drawn where PSVshell draws, a frame never waits for the plugin, and the panel is never drawn while it is being rebuilt.

## How much it gives

From my logs on a PCH-1000 with a microSD in an SD2Vita, per play session including loading screens:

- retail games: from about 0.3 to 3.5 seconds less waiting, depending on how much the game reads in order;
- homebrew ports that read files in many small pieces (GTA San Andreas, Vice City): much more, mostly from very small reads served from a block.

These are the plugin's own estimates from its log, not stopwatch measurements. Most loading is not limited by storage, so some games gain little.

## Good to know

- Tested on one console: a PCH-1000 on firmware 3.65.
- If you see error **C1-2569-2** (out of kernel memory), see the [README](https://github.com/Osaul4ik/vita-memio#error-c1-2569-2).

## Install or update

Copy `vitamemio_kernel.skprx`, `vitamemio_hud.skprx` and `vitamemio.suprx` to `ur0:tai/` and restart. Always update all three together. `vitamemio_hud.skprx` does not go in `config.txt`. For a new install, add the plugin's lines to `config.txt` first; see the [README](https://github.com/Osaul4ik/vita-memio#install).

To uninstall: switch off every storage in the plugin's settings, remove its lines from `config.txt`, restart, then delete the three files and `ur0:data/vita-memio/`.
